items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.39 at source lines 1372-1378: two continuous functions on the Cauchy reals that agree at every rational point are equal. The author's proof (source lines 1379-1394) is an induction on the Cauchy reals whose limit case requires assembling three inputs: the two continuity moduli theta and eta obtained from the hypothesis on f and g (lines 1385-1388), a comparison point y_delta which the retained cited result places close to lim(x) within both moduli once delta is chosen small (lines 1390-1391), and the inductive hypothesis f(y_delta) = g(y_delta) inserted in the middle of the chain, after which only the triangle inequality remains (lines 1392-1393). The statement mentions neither the moduli nor the auxiliary point.
